correctness.rationale: The exact boundedness condition is obtained from the established one-dimensional closed Epperson region via two-sided tensor restriction, preserving norm one on every boundary point. The vertical boundary is the pointwise maximum of two inverse-sinh sine thresholds. The period group is precisely the imaginary-axis common zero lattice. For irrational rates the time density is a torus equidistribution integral; for rational coprime rates the small-time allowed intersection is a single shrinking circular arc. The liminf contact coefficient follows from a uniform small-distance expansion about the two zero lattices and matching upper/lower Diophantine best-approximation bounds. All three mathematical limits and their quantifiers are explicit; the finite checker executes but is not relied upon as a proof.

originality.rationale: The result does not claim discovery of the two-rate norm-one criterion: Janson (1997), Theorem 2, is an already broader Gaussian second-quantization criterion that implies it. The contribution is a connected, quantitative arithmetic theorem about the resulting region, with a rational/irrational density-exponent transition and a sharp Lagrange-constant boundary-contact law. These consequences are not stated in the inspected primary papers and cannot be obtained by renaming a norm constant; they require independent equidistribution and quantitative zero-lattice approximation. The unresolved original Epperson full-text access and broader unindexed arithmetic literature are recorded as residual risks.
residual_risks: An older, unindexed arithmetic analysis of anisotropic Gaussian complex-time semigroups may already give the same exponent and contact laws.
The original Epperson 1989 full text remained inaccessible, although its Gaussian criterion is confirmed in later primary works.
The general Janson criterion is stronger on operator boundedness; originality is limited strictly to the derived arithmetic geometry, not the tensor contractivity test.

The motivating 2026-11-04 source concerns an inverse-Gaussian operator rather than the same classical Gaussian operator; the new theorem is a deliberately distinct comparison, not an extension of its theorem statements.

value.rationale: Bruno and colleagues (arXiv:2611.06826v1, 4 November 2026) highlight operator and measure dependence of Ornstein–Uhlenbeck semigroup mapping properties, making the classical Gaussian complex-time comparator a motivated model. In that natural two-rate model, irrationality of relaxation clocks changes the vanishing exponent of the bounded imaginary-time density from one to two and turns the optimal remote boundary contact into the Lagrange constant rescaled by a natural operator parameter. This gives an infinite arithmetic classification with sharp constants; neither the fixed-time norm criterion nor elementary one-rate periodicity is claimed novel.
